title: A genome-scale single-cell CRISPRi map of trans gene regulation across human pluripotent stem cell lines
A leakage-aware benchmark for evaluating chemical and cellular generalization in single-cell perturbation-response prediction
key: Leakage-aware splits that separate chemical-analogue, new-scaffold, new-context and new-mechanism generalisation for perturbation models.
findings: Reported performance depends strongly on the split; scaffold splits still leave many same-mechanism neighbours.

title: A mechanism-annotated benchmark reveals limited fidelity to drug-response signatures in single-cell perturbation models
key: scDrugPerturb-Bench: links drug perturbation profiles to curated drug-response signatures to test mechanism fidelity, not just reconstruction.
findings: Models show limited fidelity to drug-response signatures; good reconstruction is a poor proxy, and frozen FM embeddings give only local gains.

title: A Standardized Framework For Evaluating Gene Expression Generative Models
key: GGE: open-source framework of standardised distributional and DEG-focused metrics for single-cell generative models.
findings: Metric values vary substantially with implementation choices, so standardised reporting is needed.

title: A systematic assessment of single-cell language model configurations
key: bento-sc: isolates pretraining choices of single-cell language models one at a time to find which design decisions matter.
findings: scLMs do not yet beat baselines by much; best results come from minimally processed counts, count-distribution losses, high masking rates and combined objectives.

title: A Systematic Comparison of Single-Cell Perturbation Response Prediction Models
evaluates: scgpt; scfoundation; squidiff; gears; biolord; cpa
findings: PerturbNet best recovers DE signatures, but no method generalises across cell types; fine-tuned foundation models underestimate synergy.

title: A world model of the virtual cell
key: Proposes the virtual cell world model: a stateful system that simulates a cell's evolution under interventions, with an architecture, data and evaluation plan.

title: Accessible and reproducible deployment reveals the practical boundaries of single-cell foundation models
evaluates: scfoundation; scprint; scimilarity; scgpt; geneformer; cellfm; scbert; cellplm; uce; langcell; cellama; sccello; genept
findings: Usefulness is neither universal nor set by model scale; it depends on the representation, the biological context and the supervision.

title: AmbiModBench: Benchmarking Gene Perturbation Prediction Beyond Shared Responses
key: AmbiModBench: specificity-aware perturbation benchmark that separates target-specific predictions from shared background responses.
findings: Strong absolute scores mostly reflect the shared background response rather than target-specific learning.

title: An Empirical Comparison of Virtual Cell Models: Perturbation Prediction, Representation, and the Baseline Gap
key: Compares perturbation predictors, foundation-model embeddings and STATE on prediction and representation tasks against linear baselines.
evaluates: gears; cpa; geneformer; scgpt; scfoundation; uce; state
findings: Deep models gain on combinatorial perturbations, unseen cell types and especially representation tasks, but rarely beat baselines on perturbation prediction.

title: Artificial Intelligence Virtual Organoids (AIVOs)
key: Review defining AI virtual organoids: organoid-scale digital twins built from virtual cells, with architecture, construction, evaluation and applications.

title: Artificial intelligence-enabled multi-scale virtual cell: perspective, challenges, and opportunities
AssayBench: An Assay-Level Virtual Cell Benchmark for LLMs and Agents
findings: General-purpose LLMs used zero-shot beat biology-specific models and agents, but every method stays well below the estimated performance ceiling.

title: Assessing scale and predictive diversity in models for single-cell transcriptomics based on Geneformer
key: Studies architecture and pretraining scale for Geneformer-style rank-based models (GF-CAB).
findings: More pretraining data does not uniformly help; models trained on much less data can match or beat larger ones.

title: Auditing Confidence-Calibrated Benchmarking of Single-Cell Perturbation Models
key: Audits uncertainty-calibrated benchmarking of perturbation models (scVI, CPA, ridge) and documents six failure modes.
findings: Marginal coverage can look fine while covering few DE-gene intervals; conformal prediction should be recalibrated per context.

title: Auditing pretraining contamination in single-cell foundation model benchmarks
key: scContam: audits whether benchmark cells were in foundation-model pretraining data, at the cell level.
findings: Models resist memorising individual cells, but contaminated cells embed measurably more tightly, so pretraining audits should accompany benchmarks.

title: Benchmarking biological knowledge-graph priors against single-cell foundation models for Perturb-seq prediction
key: Compares biological knowledge-graph priors with single-cell foundation models for Perturb-seq prediction.

title: Benchmarking gene expression reconstruction from single-cell latent representations
key: ReconEval: benchmarks how well gene expression can be decoded back from latent spaces, from PCA and autoencoders to frozen foundation-model embeddings.
findings: Autoencoders reconstruct best at low dimension; frozen foundation-model embeddings keep recoverable gene information, but high-dimensional PCA matches them for latent perturbation modelling.

title: Benchmarking LLM-based agents for single-cell omics analysis
key: Benchmark of LLM-based agent frameworks on single-cell omics analysis tasks across omics types, species and technologies.
findings: Multi-agent frameworks beat single agents; code quality matters most, and self-reflection helps more than retrieval or planning.

title: Benchmarking single-cell foundation models for real-world RNA-seq data integration
key: Benchmarks foundation models against scVI and Harmony for integrating 1.5M clinical and preclinical cells, with robustness rankings.
findings: Fine-tuning helps, but scVI is the best overall integrator.

title: Benchmarking single-cell foundation models in a zero-shot setting
key: Zero-shot evaluation of four foundation models on annotation, protein-expression prediction and integration.
findings: Baselines win most annotation and integration tasks; foundation embeddings help for protein prediction (SCimilarity, TranscriptFormer).

title: Benchmarking single-cell foundation models reveals an advantage in the low-data regime for cell-type and disease-state prediction
key: Benchmarks four foundation-model representations on 868 disease-prediction and 65 cell-type tasks from CELLxGENE.
findings: With full data, log-normalised counts match or beat the best model; with about 100 labelled cells per class or fewer, TranscriptFormer wins.

title: Benchmarking Static Gene Regulatory Network Reconstruction and Dynamic Transition Probing in Single-Cell Foundation Models
key: Benchmarks regulatory networks recovered from token embeddings, hidden states and attention of six foundation models, and adds dynamic transition probing.
findings: scGPT token embeddings beat classical GRN baselines and scFoundation best reproduces developmental transitions; what can be recovered depends on architecture and extraction.

title: Benchmarking virtual cell models for in-the-wild perturbation response
key: Standardized, modular benchmark for virtual cell perturbation prediction under unseen cell contexts, unseen perturbations, and cross-dataset generalization; finds performance is highly context-dependent and often overestimated in standard setups.
evaluates: state; sclambda; prnet; biolord; cpa; sams-vae; gears
findings: Performance is often overestimated and drops sharply under stricter context shifts; models capture global trends but miss perturbation-specific effects.

title: Benchmarking zero-shot single-cell foundation model embeddings for cellular dynamics reconstruction
key: Benchmarks zero-shot foundation-model embeddings for reconstructing trajectories from time-resolved single-cell data.
findings: The HVG baseline beats foundation embeddings; the models over-compress temporal signal and flatten branches.

title: Beyond Expression Prediction: Benchmarking Differential Expression Classification in Single-Cell Perturbation Models
key: Evaluates perturbation models on predicting differential-expression outcomes for unseen perturbations and unseen cell lines.
findings: Simple baselines like embedding nearest neighbours are competitive or better; sparsity calibration helps deep models.

title: Beyond the Final Layer: Evaluating Single-Cell Foundation Model Representations for Molecular Prediction
key: Layer-wise probing of four foundation models as frozen feature extractors for cell-type and perturbation prediction, with readout and geometry diagnostics.
findings: Intermediate layers often beat the final layer for scGPT and scBERT cell-type tasks; the best depth depends on model, task and readout.

title: Can We Trust In-Distribution Success? Locked Evaluation Reveals Transfer Failure and Sampling-Depth Entanglement in CRISPRi Perturbation Prediction
key: Pre-registered, locked evaluation of a frozen Geneformer representation for CRISPRi perturbation-effect prediction.
findings: In-distribution success does not transfer, and the challenge endpoint is strongly tied to cell count.

title: Causal circuit tracing reveals distinct computational architectures in single-cell foundation models: inhibitory dominance, biological coherence, and cross-model convergence
key: Ablates sparse-autoencoder features one at a time in Geneformer and scGPT to map model-internal causal circuits and compares them with known regulation.
findings: The circuits are reproducible and enriched for known biology and ChIP-seq-supported TF targets, but largely mirror co-expression.

title: Causal intervention validation of gene regulatory signals in scGPT
key: Ablates or swaps transcription-factor tokens inside scGPT, traces circuits with activation patching, and checks the resulting edges against curated references and CRISPR data.

title: Cell shapes decode molecular phenotypes in image-based spatial proteomics
CLAMP: Steady-State ODE Inference of Gene Regulatory Networks from Single-Cell Perturbations
key: Fits one shared steady-state ODE to Perturb-seq data through a frozen foundation-model encoder, so recovery of the regulatory network measures how much regulatory structure the encoder keeps.
findings: Each foundation-model encoder loses regulatory structure in its own way: some cannot keep regulatory directions separable, others keep them only non-linearly.

title: Context-dependent utility and robustness of pretrained single-cell foundation model representations across analytical tasks
key: Zero-shot evaluation of 20 representation methods on 6 tasks and 1,607 datasets, testing both utility and robustness to changes in dataset structure.
findings: No method wins across tasks, top performers are often fragile to dataset changes, and simple statistical methods stay competitive.

title: Decoding Conserved and Tissue-Specific Cellular Stress Programs from Single-Cell Foundation Models Using Sparse Autoencoders
key: Uses sparse autoencoders on foundation-model embeddings of a multi-organ ageing atlas to extract cellular stress programs.
findings: The features recover known and new stress programs, some conserved across tissues and increasingly co-active with age, others tissue-specific.

title: Discovery of a Hematopoietic Manifold in scGPT Yields a Method for Extracting Performant Algorithms from Biological Foundation Model Internals
key: Finds a hematopoietic manifold inside scGPT and exports it from frozen attention weights as a compact standalone algorithm.
findings: The extracted algorithm orders pseudotime best against scVI, Palantir and others, with about 1000-fold fewer trainable parameters than probing.

title: Dissecting the Virtual Cell: A Review of Mechanistic Interpretability for Single-cell Biological Foundation Models
key: Review of mechanistic interpretability methods applied to single-cell foundation models.

title: Do Geometric Outliers Identify Important Genes in Single-Cell Foundation Models?
key: Screens Geneformer, scGPT and scFoundation gene embeddings for geometric outliers and tests whether those genes matter for annotation or disease.
findings: The models agree only weakly on outlier genes, and outliers neither drive cell-type annotation nor mark disease genes; embedding geometry is mostly model-specific.

title: Evaluating Single-Cell Perturbation Response Models Is Far from Straightforward
key: Stress-tests perturbation models and their metrics with cross-splitting, controlled noise and synthetic data.
findings: Common correlation and distribution metrics are swayed by scale, sparsity and dimension; complex models often trail simple baselines on chemical perturbation data.

title: Evaluating the ability of spatial transcriptomics foundation models to learn multi-scale spatial variation
key: SAFFRON: uses Matryoshka sparse autoencoders on spatial foundation-model embeddings to test whether they capture local and global spatial variation.
findings: Novae captures global spatial gradients better than simple baselines, but no spatial model beats baselines on local microenvironment patterns.

title: Evaluating the learnability of single-cell large language models on multiple tasks
key: Tests whether larger models and more data help Geneformer and scGPT on perturbation prediction and annotation, using real and synthetic data.
findings: Scaling gives little or even hurts; for perturbation prediction the models seem to capture little beyond summary statistics.

title: Evaluating the role of pretraining dataset size and diversity on single-cell foundation model performance
findings: Performance plateaus with a fraction of current corpora; there are no clear data scaling laws.

title: Evaluating the utilities of foundation models in single-cell data analysis
findings: Foundation models do not consistently beat task-specific methods; scGPT, Geneformer and CellFM come out on top.

title: Evaluation protocol choices dominate reported performance in gene regulatory network benchmarks for single-cell foundation models
key: Decomposes GRN evaluation for scGPT attention networks into symbol mapping, gold standard, candidate set and label noise.
findings: Protocol choices shift AUPR by orders of magnitude; under universe-aware scoring scGPT attention falls below random, while GENIE3 and GRNBoost2 do better.

title: Exhaustive Circuit Mapping of a Single-Cell Foundation Model Reveals Massive Redundancy, Heavy-Tailed Hub Architecture, and Layer-Dependent Differentiation Control
key: Traces every active sparse-autoencoder feature in one Geneformer layer, tests higher-order ablations and steers cell trajectories with features.
findings: Exhaustive tracing reveals a heavy-tailed hub structure missed by selective sampling and strong redundancy; late-layer features push cells toward maturity.

title: Fifteen challenges for generative AI applications to cell biology
key: Fifteen grand challenges, modelled on Hilbert's problems, for generative AI in cell biology.

title: Foundation Models for Single-cell Biology: A Review of Architectures, Benchmarks, and the Push toward Mechanistic Understanding
key: Review of single-cell foundation model architectures and benchmarks, and of the move toward mechanistic understanding.

title: Foundation models improve perturbation response prediction
key: Compares 600+ models for embedding-based perturbation response prediction; some foundation models beat simple baselines, and combining several helps.

title: From Equations to Agents: The Artificial Intelligence Virtual Cell Reshaping Precision Oncology
From modality-specific to compositional foundation models for cell biology
key: Argues for compositional, modular foundation models that join chromatin, protein, spatial, imaging and text modalities on the way to agentic virtual cells.

title: Genetic Perturbation Prediction Models Fail Out-of-Distribution: A Rigorous Benchmark and Systematic Evaluation
key: EL-PERTURB: stress-tests 20 perturbation models under stratified out-of-distribution splits on essential-gene and genome-wide screens.
findings: Performance drops sharply out of distribution, and complexity, including foundation-model embeddings, gives no reliable advantage.

title: Harmonised benchmarking of foundation models for single-cell and spatial transcriptomics reveals context-dependent generalisation
key: Harmonised benchmark of six single-cell and spatial foundation models across scRNA-seq, spatial and Perturb-seq tasks.
evaluates: nicheformer; cellplm; scgpt-spatial; genept; scelmo; novae
findings: No model dominates: cell-level transformers lead identity tasks, spatial models preserve tissue structure, and language-derived gene embeddings compete on some perturbation metrics.

title: How different AI models understand cells differently
key: scGeneLens: sparsifies attention, propagates it across layers and applies integrated gradients to see which gene relations scFoundation and scGPT rely on.
findings: scFoundation leans on cell-type marker relations (sharper cell-type separation), while scGPT leans on shared pathway genes (better transfer across conditions).

title: How Much Information Is Stored in Single-Cell Foundation Models, and How Much Can Be Extracted? A Review of Probing, Interpretability, and the Limits of Representation Readout
key: Review of probing and interpretability for single-cell foundation models and of how much stored information can actually be read out.

title: Interpretation, extrapolation and perturbation of single cells
Large-scale proteome inference from unpaired single-cell transcriptomic and proteomic data by msInfer
LLM4Cell: Taxonomy and Evaluation of LLM and Agentic Models for Single-Cell Biology
key: LLM4Cell: survey and taxonomy of 58 language-model and agentic systems for single-cell biology, mapped to tasks, datasets and ten evaluation dimensions.

title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Biological Foundation Models: An Empirical Analysis of scGPT Gene-Embedding Geometry
key: Empirical analysis of the geometry of scGPT gene embeddings.

title: Minimal life by computer
Multi-Dimensional Spectral Geometry of Biological Knowledge in Single-Cell Transformer Representations
key: Automated hypothesis screening of the spectral geometry of scGPT gene representations across layers.
findings: scGPT arranges genes along interpretable axes (subcellular location, protein interactions, regulator versus target), with detail that changes across depth.

title: MVCBench: A Multimodal Benchmark for Drug-induced Virtual Cell Phenotypes
evaluates: tgpt; scfoundation; scgpt; geneformer; cellplm; scbert; uce; state; cell2sentence; scimilarity
findings: Performance collapses under distribution shift; adding morphology to transcriptomics consistently helps.

title: OmniVCBench: Benchmarking Evidence-Grounded Multimodal Reasoning Towards AI Virtual Cells
key: OmniVCBench: figure-centred benchmark of how multimodal models interpret experimental evidence and form hypotheses toward AI virtual cells.

title: Parameter-free representations outperform single-cell foundation models on downstream benchmarks
key: Asks whether careful normalisation plus linear methods can match foundation models on their own benchmarks.
findings: Simple linear pipelines reach state-of-the-art or near it, and beat foundation models on out-of-distribution cell types and species.

title: Partial-label metric ceilings for evaluating gene regulatory networks inferred from single-cell foundation models
key: Derives the best achievable GRN scores given incomplete reference networks and re-reads benchmark results, including attention and gradient edges from scGPT.
findings: Incomplete references explain only part of the gap: even the leading scGPT probes stay far below the achievable ceiling.

title: PertDiffBench: Benchmarking Diffusion Models for Single-Cell Perturbation Response Prediction
key: PertDiffBench: benchmarks diffusion models for perturbation response under varied tasks, representations and stress tests.
findings: Results depend heavily on task and representation; pretrained encoders don't consistently help, with scVI slightly ahead of STATE.

title: PertReason: A Knowledge-Grounded Benchmark and Framework for Cell-State-Conditioned Mechanistic Reasoning of Perturbation Effects
key: PertReason: benchmark of mechanistically faithful, cell-state-conditioned reasoning about perturbation effects, with a reference model.
findings: Models often get correct answers through flawed logic or ignore cellular context.

title: Re-evaluating the benefit of pretraining scale in cell foundation models
key: Re-tests data scaling for first- and second-generation cell foundation models with standard and fully frozen fine-tuning.
findings: Scaling benefits appear once evaluation is fully frozen, so fine-tuning saturation does not mean the representations saturate.

title: Reference-cell design shapes model evaluation in single-cell perturbation prediction
key: Shows how the choice and allocation of control (reference) cells changes perturbation benchmark results.
findings: Reassigning control cells can reverse model rankings without changing any model or metric.

title: Regulatory Logic in Larger Single-Cell Foundation Models: A Sparse Autoencoder Comparison of scFoundation and Geneformer
key: Compares sparse-autoencoder features of scFoundation and Geneformer for pathway alignment, sparsity and response to transcription-factor perturbation.
findings: scFoundation's features align more often with known regulatory modules and are less polysemantic than Geneformer's.

title: Representing biological concepts as directions in foundation model embeddings
key: Concept activation vectors: linear directions in protein and single-cell foundation-model embeddings that represent biological properties.
findings: Linear concept directions recover functional annotations in protein embeddings and cancer-associated transitions in single-cell embeddings.

title: Rethinking Class Imbalance for Single-Cell Foundation Models: A Systematic Benchmark Across Architectures and Long-Tail Loss Functions
key: Benchmarks six long-tail loss functions across three foundation models for rare cell types.
findings: Some rare classes are recoverable with the right loss, others are absorbed under every loss; class-balanced loss and LDAM are the most consistent.

title: Revisiting the blueprint for an interpretable virtual cell
key: Short piece revisiting systems biology as a blueprint for an interpretable virtual cell.

title: Robustness to nuisance perturbations enables unsupervised evaluation of single-cell foundation models
key: Unsupervised evaluation: checks whether embeddings keep their neighbourhood structure under small technical and sampling perturbations.
findings: Models that tie on standard benchmarks differ almost twofold in stability after dropping 5% of counts.

title: SC-Arena: A Natural Language Benchmark for Single-Cell Reasoning with Knowledge-Augmented Evaluation
key: SC-Arena: natural-language benchmark of single-cell reasoning with knowledge-augmented evaluation.
findings: LLMs perform unevenly on tasks needing mechanistic or causal understanding.

title: Scaling recipes for single-cell RNA sequencing foundation models: when do scaling laws hold?
key: Trains families of single-cell foundation models to measure how pretraining loss scales with size and compute, and how to set learning rate and depth.
findings: Pretraining loss follows a power law in model size and compute, with strength depending on the model formulation; optimal learning rate and depth-to-width ratio scale predictably.

title: scArchon: a scalable benchmarking framework for assessing single-cell perturbation models
key: scArchon: a reproducible Snakemake platform for benchmarking single-cell perturbation-prediction tools with statistical and biological metrics.
findings: trVAE, scGen, scPRAM and scVIDR are robust across datasets, others sometimes trail linear or control baselines, and good scores can still miss key perturbation signatures.

title: scCluBench: Comprehensive Benchmarking of Clustering Algorithms for Single-Cell RNA Sequencing
SCMBench: benchmarking domain-specific and foundation models for single-cell multi-omics data integration
key: SCMBench: benchmarks domain-specific and foundation models for single-cell multi-omics integration, beyond accuracy to biomarkers, regulatory elements and trajectories.
findings: Foundation models generally fall short of the best domain-specific models; a lightweight adaptation narrows the gap.

title: Scoring gene importance by interpreting single-cell foundation models
key: SIGnature: scores each gene's importance in a cell from foundation-model attributions and searches large atlases with those scores.
findings: Attribution scores are a cleaner, comparable measure of gene importance than expression; an atlas search linked the MS1 monocyte program to Kawasaki disease.

title: Signal, Bounds, and Baselines: Principles for Evaluating Virtual Cell Perturbation Models
key: Proposes three evaluation principles: DEG-aware signal checks, calibration against empirical bounds, and a ladder of linear baselines.
findings: Deep models, including foundation models, often fail to meaningfully beat simple linear baselines, and leave much room for improvement even where they do.

title: Sparse autoencoders reveal interpretable cell-type programs in single-cell foundation model representations
key: Trains sparse autoencoders on every scGPT layer for immune cells and checks the features against cell types, gene sets and PCA.
findings: Later-layer features recover coherent cell-type programs, but sparsity needs calibrating to avoid many dead features.

title: Sparse autoencoders reveal organized biological knowledge but minimal regulatory logic in single-cell foundation models: a comparative atlas of Geneformer and scGPT
key: Trains TopK sparse autoencoders on Geneformer V2 and scGPT activations and releases interactive atlases of 107,000+ interpretable features; finds organized biological knowledge but minimal regulatory logic.
findings: The models encode organized pathway and module knowledge but almost no causal regulatory logic.

title: Spatial perturb-seq: single-cell functional genomics within intact tissue architecture
Spectral universality in single-cell foundation models: a low-dimensional shared core carries the biology
key: Compares the gene-embedding subspaces of seven transcriptome models and a protein language model to find what they share.
findings: The models agree little overall, but share a small core subspace that carries nearly all the biology; the rest is model-specific.

title: Systematic evaluation of single-cell foundation model interpretability: attention-derived edge scores add no incremental value over gene-level features for perturbation-target prediction
key: Tests whether attention-derived gene-gene edges in scGPT and Geneformer carry regulatory information, with ablations and trivial baselines across cell types and CRISPR modalities.
findings: Attention maps carry layer-specific biological structure, but add nothing beyond simple gene-level statistics for predicting perturbation targets.

title: Tabular Foundation Models Are Competitive Cellular Perturbation Predictors Across Biological Scales
key: Compares general-purpose tabular foundation models (TabPFN, TabICL) with specialised single-cell perturbation models across cell lines, primary T cells and zebrafish embryos.
findings: Off-the-shelf tabular foundation models match or beat specialised single-cell models, most clearly on pseudobulk perturbation prediction.

title: Task-dependent Performance of Single-cell Foundation Models under Low Supervision
key: Benchmark evaluating single-cell foundation models under low-supervision (limited-label) scenarios.
evaluates: cellplm; scmulan; nicheformer; scfoundation; geneformer; langcell; scgpt
findings: CellPLM leads clustering, annotation and batch correction, scMulan leads perturbation, and PCA leads reconstruction.

title: The 2026 Virtual Cell Challenge: predicting perturbation responses in cell contexts a model has never seen
key: Announces the 2026 Virtual Cell Challenge: a zero-shot task predicting CRISPRi knockdown responses in six cell lines never seen perturbed, with no training set released.

title: The Landscape of Single-Cell Foundation Models: Design Principles, Applications, and Open Challenges
key: Review of single-cell foundation models by data representation, architecture and objective, with applications and open challenges.

title: Toward trustworthy virtual cells: a roadmap for perturbation-resolved, context-aware, and experimentally validated cell models
venue: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
key: Roadmap for trustworthy virtual cells that are perturbation-resolved, context-aware and experimentally validated, with evaluation beyond held-out reconstruction.

title: Towards Autonomous Mechanistic Reasoning in Virtual Cells
Towards predictive virtual embryos with genomics and AI
Towards principled evaluation of single-cell perturbation prediction models
key: Taxonomy of perturbation-prediction evaluation (representation, metric, score transformation, reporting) with scPertEval, a package of reference protocols.
findings: Benchmarks disagree largely because their evaluation choices differ; making those choices explicit is a precondition for comparable results.

title: VCBench: A Multi-Dimensional Benchmark for Single-Cell Foundation Models
key: Scores foundation models on five testable virtual-cell capabilities (perturbation, cross-species, GRN, modality integration, temporal order) against pre-registered baselines.
findings: Linear and nearest-neighbour baselines match or beat every model on four of five dimensions; TranscriptFormer leads RNA-to-protein prediction but loses temporal ordering.

title: Virtual cell construction for artificial intelligence‐driven drug discovery
key: Review of virtual-cell modelling paradigms and how they support target prioritisation, drug response and combination design.

title: Virtual Cell Models Inflate Perturbation Effect Sizes and Undermine Causal Gene Regulatory Network Recovery
key: PerturbCausal: runs causal network discovery on virtual-cell model predictions to test whether they preserve regulatory structure, against a sparse linear baseline.
findings: No deep virtual-cell model beat a sparse linear baseline at recovering causal networks; predicted effects were inflated and nearly uniform across perturbations, and calibration did not fix it.

title: Virtual cell: Current perspectives and future prospects
key: Overview of virtual-cell technology, from classic simulation platforms to AI models, with applications and challenges.

title: Virtual Cells Need Context, Not Just Scale
Virtual-cell models compress unseen intervention geometry through a target-specific generalization bottleneck
key: Analyses the geometry of perturbation-model outputs to explain why accurate-looking predictions for unseen interventions lose what distinguishes them.
findings: Models reconstruct cell states for unseen interventions yet collapse the geometry that separates them; anchoring each intervention with a little real data helps most.

title: What Do Biological Foundation Models Compute? Sparse Autoencoders from Feature Recovery to Mechanistic Interpretability
key: Systematic review of sparse autoencoders across protein, genomic, pathology and single-cell foundation models, and how their features are validated.

title: What Makes a Representation Good for Single-Cell Perturbation Prediction?
What Makes a Virtual Cell a World Model? Three Gaps, Three Experiments, and a Roadmap
key: Defines virtual cell world models through three gaps (dynamics, intervention, scale), backs them with three experiments and gives a capability ladder.

title: What topological and geometric structure do biological foundation models learn? Evidence from 141 hypotheses
key: Uses an AI-driven hypothesis loop to test 141 topological and geometric hypotheses about scGPT and Geneformer gene embeddings, with null controls.
findings: Both models learn real, shared structure in gene space, but agree on its shape rather than on gene placement, and much of the signal is tissue-specific.

title: When Does Gene Regulatory Network Inference Break? A Controlled Diagnostic Study of Causal and Correlational Methods on Single-Cell Data
key: Controlled simulation study that turns up one pathology at a time (dropout, confounders, feedback, density and more) to see where causal and correlational GRN inference fail.
findings: Causal methods win in clean, structurally favourable settings, but dropout and latent confounders erase their advantage.

title: World models for biomedicine
key: Proposes world models for biomedicine that simulate biological trajectories under alternative interventions, from molecules to patients.

title: ‘Virtual cells’ aim to turn raw data into predictive models of biology
key: Nature news feature on the push to build virtual cells that turn raw data into predictive models of biology.

title: A genome-wide atlas of human cell morphology
A Simple and Comprehensive Benchmark for Single-Cell Transcriptomics
key: Benchmark addressing long-tailed data, model choice and evaluation for transcriptomic models, with fair downstream tasks.
findings: Weighted sampling helps consistently, and transformers are not the only competitive architecture.

title: A survey on foundation language models for single-cell biology
A Systematic Evaluation of Single-Cell Foundation Models on Cell-Type Classification Task
findings: scFoundation is consistently best, while Geneformer sometimes falls below the baselines.

title: AI-driven virtual cell models in preclinical research: technical pathways, validation mechanisms, and clinical translation potential
key: review outlines the technical pathways and validation mechanisms of virtual cells, emphasizing a closed-loop workflow from computational evaluation to experimental verification using CRISPR assays and organoid platforms.

title: Artificial Intelligence Virtual Cells: From Measurements to Decisions across Modality, Scale, Dynamics, and Evaluation
AUPRC: a metric for evaluating the performance of in-silico perturbation methods in identifying differentially expressed genes
key: Proposes AUPRC on differentially expressed genes as an evaluation metric for in-silico perturbation models.
findings: Models with high R² often fail to identify DE genes, so R² alone overstates performance.

title: Batch Effects Remain a Fundamental Barrier to Universal Embeddings in Single-Cell Foundation Models
Benchmarking algorithms for generalizable single-cell perturbation response prediction
findings: Across 27 methods and 29 datasets, generalising to unseen contexts calls for better cell-context embeddings.

title: Benchmarking and Evaluation of AI Models in Biology: Outcomes and Recommendations from the CZI Virtual Cells Workshop
Benchmarking cell type and gene set annotation by large language models with AnnDictionary
findings: LLMs annotate major cell types with over 80-90% accuracy, and agreement grows with model size.

title: Benchmarking foundation cell models for post-perturbation RNA-seq prediction
key: Benchmarks scGPT and scFoundation against simple baselines for predicting post-perturbation expression on Perturb-seq data.
findings: Even predicting the training mean beat both foundation models, and simple models with biological features beat scGPT by a wide margin; common Perturb-seq benchmarks have little perturbation-specific variance.

title: Benchmarking gene embeddings from sequence, expression, network, and text models for functional prediction tasks
findings: The type of training data matters more than how an embedding is built; sequence-based embeddings suit genetic interactions, expression-based ones disease associations.

title: Benchmarking large language models for cell typing in single-cell RNA-Seq
key: Benchmarks seven LLMs and three classical tools for cell-type annotation on 34 human and mouse datasets (DeepCellSeek).
findings: LLMs clearly beat traditional methods, especially for fine subtypes, and an ensemble of the top models does best.

title: Benchmarking Machine Learning Models for Cellular Perturbation Analysis
BioLLM: A standardized framework for integrating and benchmarking single-cell foundation models
findings: scGPT is the most robust overall; scBERT lags.

title: Biology-driven insights into the power of single-cell foundation models
findings: No single foundation model wins every task; simpler models adapt better under limited resources.

title: BMFM-RNA: whole-cell expression decoding improves transcriptomic foundation models
key: Open framework for building/evaluating transcriptomic FMs.

title: Build the virtual cell with artificial intelligence: a perspective for cancer research
CIGS: High-Throughput Profiling of Chemical-Induced Gene Expression across 93,644 Perturbations
Deep Learning-Based Genetic Perturbation Models Do Outperform Uninformative Baselines on Well-Calibrated Metrics
findings: Under well-calibrated metrics deep models do beat mean and linear baselines; earlier reports of underperformance came from poorly calibrated metrics such as MSE.

title: Deep-learning-based gene perturbation effect prediction does not yet outperform simple linear baselines
evaluates: scfoundation; scgpt; uce; scbert; geneformer; gears; cpa
findings: None of the five foundation models beat simple linear baselines at predicting perturbation effects.
